result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returns `response` (a raw fetch `Response`) when credential sharing is enabled (`return response;` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`). In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff adds `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` followed by `const token = res?.data;` — a raw fetch Response has no `data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` on the next line throws. The mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff; the non-sync path returns `fetchTokens.res` which does have `.data`, confirming the discrepancy.

judged_text: The code reads `const token = res?.data` but in credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, which has no `data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh on a credential-sharing deployment crashes before persisting, taking down booking calendar operations with an unhandled TypeError instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, credential-sharing mode returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object. But `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still treats the return value like an axios/gaxios-style object and does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime when credential sharing is enabled.
